modules.title: Vision analysis in Foundry
modules.summary: Deepens computer vision coverage with OCR, tags, captions, image-analysis design, and responsible review patterns.

lessons.title: Analyze images with Foundry vision capabilities
lessons.summary: Go deeper on computer vision scenarios in Foundry: image analysis, OCR, tags, captions, and responsible-use boundaries.
learningObjectives: Choose OCR, tags, captions, or object detection based on an image question
Explain how confidence scores and blur affect review decisions
Identify privacy limits when extracting metadata from uploaded images
lessons.explanation:
Imagine Relecloud receives thousands of luggage photos after a storm. Some show damaged handles, some show readable tags, and some are too blurry to trust. **Computer vision** helps an app interpret those images, but the feature depends on the question.

Use **OCR** when the app must read text such as a baggage tag, serial number, sign, or printed form. Use **image tags** for broad labels such as suitcase, airport, or queue. Use **captions** when a human-readable sentence is useful, such as an accessibility description. Use **object detection** when the app must locate items in an image.

Foundry Tools documentation describes Azure Vision image analysis and OCR capabilities, while AI-901 expects candidates to recognize vision and image-generation workloads. The design habit is to avoid asking vision to do more than needed. A catalog app might need OCR and captions, not identity recognition. A claims workflow might use confidence signals and route unclear cases to human review.

Vision is sensitive to blur, lighting, angle, handwriting, languages, and occlusion. Responsible use means testing with representative images, explaining uncertainty, and limiting sensitive decisions unless the workflow includes oversight.

terminology.definition: A vision capability that extracts printed or handwritten text from images or documents.
Assigning labels to objects, actions, or scenes detected in an image.
Generating a sentence that describes visual content.
Finding and locating objects in an image.
A value that estimates how reliable a detected or extracted result is.

lessons.businessScenario: Relecloud builds a baggage-claim assistant. Travelers upload a damaged bag and tag photo. The assistant reads the tag, adds visual tags, creates an accessible caption, and sends unclear images to an agent.
lessons.technicalExample: A lightweight flow accepts a JPEG, calls OCR for `BagTagNumber`, calls image analysis for tags and a caption, stores only required metadata, and displays `OCR confidence low; ask for review`.

misconception.myth: If a model returns a caption, the caption is a verified fact.
misconception.reality: Captions and tags are model outputs. Treat them as useful signals that may need confidence checks, user confirmation, or human review.

lessons.examTakeaway: If the requirement says read text, choose OCR. If it says describe an image, choose captions. If it says identify visual concepts, choose tags or object detection.
lessons.recap: Vision workloads turn images into text, tags, captions, locations, or extracted fields. Choose the smallest capability that meets the scenario.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Vision services are like different pairs of glasses: one reads words, one notices objects, and one describes the scene.
lessons.anotherExample: Wide World Importers photographs warehouse shelves. OCR reads bin labels, tags identify product types, and captions help workers search photos.

modules.title: Image generation in Foundry
modules.summary: Explains prompt-driven image generation, fast-changing model choices, parameters, content filters, and review workflows.

lessons.title: Generate images with Foundry models safely
lessons.summary: Learn how image-generation models create visual outputs from prompts, how parameters affect outputs, and why safety review matters.
learningObjectives: Explain when a prompt-to-image model fits a visual creation scenario
Describe how prompt details, model, size, quality, and count affect generated images
Apply content filters and review before using generated visuals
lessons.explanation:
Relecloud's design team wants quick concept art for a fictional travel campaign. They are not trying to read or classify an existing image; they want to **create** new visuals. That is the image-generation workload.

In Microsoft Foundry, image-generation models create images from text prompts and, depending on the model, optional image inputs. The prompt should describe subject, composition, style, context, and constraints. Parameters such as output size, quality, and number of images depend on the selected model and API. Model names and availability change quickly, so production guidance should be verified against current Microsoft Learn documentation.

Safety is part of the design. Content filtering works alongside models and image generation, but filters do not replace human judgment. Teams should avoid prompts that request real people, protected brands, sensitive attributes, misleading evidence, or unsafe scenarios. They should review outputs before publishing, especially for brand, public, or regulated uses.

For exam scenarios, separate **visual understanding** from **visual creation**. OCR, tags, and captions interpret an existing image. Image generation creates a new image. A responsible solution combines clear prompts, appropriate model selection, safe configuration, content filtering, and approval.

terminology.definition: Creating new visual content from text prompts and optional image inputs.
Instructions that describe what the model should produce.
A setting such as output size, quality, or number of images when supported.
A safety system that classifies prompts or outputs for harmful content categories.
A process where a person checks generated content before it is trusted or published.

lessons.businessScenario: Relecloud wants campaign mockups for an internal pitch. The team uses fictional scenes only, avoids real customers and competitor logos, generates variations, and requires approval before any image leaves the design workspace.
lessons.technicalExample: A safe request object might include `prompt`, `modelDeployment`, `size`, `quality`, `n`, `safetyReviewRequired: true`, and `blockedTerms`. The app stores prompt history for review.

misconception.myth: Content filters mean generated images are automatically safe to publish.
misconception.reality: Filters reduce risk but do not understand every brand, legal, accessibility, or context issue. Human review is still needed.

lessons.examTakeaway: If the scenario says create a new picture, choose image generation. If it says read, describe, tag, or locate things in an existing image, choose computer vision.
lessons.recap: Image generation turns prompts into new visuals. Good solutions use clear prompts, supported parameters, content filtering, and human review.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Image generation is like briefing a designer who works fast. The clearer and safer the brief, the better the drafts; you still check them before printing posters.
lessons.anotherExample: Northwind Traders generates fictional product-background ideas, forbids real celebrity likenesses, logs prompts, and routes each image to brand review.

modules.title: Information extraction in Foundry
modules.summary: Explores Content Understanding and Document Intelligence for extracting fields from documents, images, audio, and video.

lessons.title: Extract multimodal information with Content Understanding
lessons.summary: Explore how Content Understanding and Document Intelligence turn documents, forms, images, audio, and video into structured fields with confidence signals.
learningObjectives: Explain how analyzers and schemas extract structured fields from multimodal content
Choose Content Understanding or Document Intelligence from content type and layout
Use confidence scores to route low-certainty fields for human review
lessons.explanation:
Fabrikam's claims team does not need another pile of files; it needs reliable fields such as policy number, incident date, repair estimate, call reason, and visible damage notes. **Information extraction** turns messy content into structured data that an app can validate, route, or analyze.

Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools processes multiple content types, including documents, images, audio, and video, into a user-defined output format. The core idea is an **analyzer**: a configuration that defines how content is processed, which fields are extracted, and which model deployments are used. A **schema** describes fields such as `invoiceTotal`, `customerName`, or `sceneSummary`.

For structured documents, Azure Document Intelligence remains important. It provides document analysis, prebuilt models, custom models, and typed fields for forms and documents. Content Understanding extends the pattern to multimodal and generative scenarios, including audio and video, while providing structured output, confidence scores, and grounding.

Do not design extraction as blind automation. Confidence scores estimate reliability, and grounding points reviewers back to source evidence. High-confidence routine fields can flow straight through if policy allows; low-confidence or high-impact fields should be reviewed.

terminology.definition: A Foundry Tools capability for extracting structured information from documents, images, audio, and video.
A configuration that controls how content is processed and fields are extracted.
The target field structure for extracted output.
Links from extracted values back to source evidence in the content.
A Foundry Tools service for OCR and intelligent document processing with prebuilt and custom models.

lessons.businessScenario: Fabrikam receives claim packets with forms, photos, calls, and inspection clips. The team creates analyzers, exports JSON for the claims app, and requires approval for low-confidence estimates.
lessons.technicalExample: An extraction result might include `{ "policyNumber": { "value": "PX-1049", "confidence": 0.96 }, "repairEstimate": { "value": 1240.50, "confidence": 0.62, "reviewRequired": true } }`.

misconception.myth: Information extraction is just OCR with a different name.
misconception.reality: OCR reads text. Information extraction can use OCR plus layout, schemas, analyzers, classification, confidence, grounding, and multimodal reasoning.

lessons.examTakeaway: When the scenario says extract fields from forms, documents, images, audio, or video into JSON-like output, think Content Understanding or Document Intelligence.
lessons.recap: Information extraction converts unstructured or semistructured content into structured fields. Confidence and grounding guide automation and review.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Imagine a clerk reading a claim packet and filling a spreadsheet. OCR reads words; extraction decides which words belong in which cells and marks cells that need a second look.
lessons.anotherExample: Adventure Works uses Document Intelligence for tax forms, while Content Understanding summarizes an uploaded product video and extracts safety certifications.
